documents.title: GenAI Syllabus Statements
documents.summary: Provost-and-Senate guidance on GenAI syllabus statements. It sets a default that GenAI needs written instructor permission and is scholastic dishonesty otherwise, then gives instructors required elements and two sample statements (prohibited, permitted) to adapt.
documents.stance_why: The page opens "Instructors at the University may allow or prohibit the use of Generative AI (GenAI) tools in their courses", and offers a prohibited template and a permitted template; it hands the decision to instructors, so the stance is delegates with two tiers.

units.why: The passage says instructors "may allow or prohibit" GenAI in their courses, so the decision sits with each instructor, which is P04 (per-instructor rule), not a university-wide stance.
units.anchor: Instructors at the University may allow or prohibit the use of Generative AI (GenAI) tools

units.why: Instructors are "strongly encouraged to include a clear syllabus statement", which asks for an AI statement in the syllabus (P09); "strongly encouraged" makes it should rather than must.
units.anchor: strongly encouraged to include a clear syllabus statement outlining their expectations

units.why: This says what a course policy "should define", i.e. the content of the syllabus AI statement, so P09 fits better than P04 because it does not say who decides.
units.anchor: should define acceptable and unacceptable uses of GenAI, reference relevant academic policies
units.policy: A well-crafted course policy defines acceptable and unacceptable uses of GenAI, references relevant academic policies, and supports students in reaching compliance.

units.why: "Students should consult their instructors if they are unsure" is the ask-when-unsure rule (P10).
units.anchor: Students should consult their instructors if they are unsure what constitutes acceptable use

units.why: The page states it was "developed in collaboration with the Senate Committee on Educational Policy", which says by whom the guidance was made (P84).
units.anchor: developed in collaboration with the Senate Committee on Educational Policy
units.fit_note: Only names the co-developing body; no date or consultation process.

units.why: AI in coursework "requires written instructor permission", so it is off unless the instructor says yes. That is a default-when-silent rule (P06); P01 does not fit because the instructor can grant permission. Final codes after reconciliation: actor=student, phase=during-work, modality=must, policy_type=P06, unit_stance=restrict.
units.anchor: Use of generative artificial intelligence as part of coursework requires written instructor permission
